proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed hypothesis is sup_k (‖u_k‖_{L¹(W)} + ∫_W |Du_k|) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U; the frozen contract places the constant |Du_k|(W) inside the integrand, and this step recovers the printed unweighted bound. The argument below is step A0 of the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1 (Section A of the parent root.bv_results-a1), specialized to this self-contained statement with the details filled in. Notation: ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume (Lebesgue measure), ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral in [0,∞], ‖a‖ₑ ∈ [0,∞) the extended norm, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Statement recalled. W ⊆ ℝⁿ is open with μ(W) < ∞, u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ), b_k := Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W ∈ [0,∞] (an x-independent constant), and S := ⨆_k ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + b_k) dx < ∞ (the whole sum is the integrand). We must find a real c ≥ 0 with ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ ofReal c and b_k ≤ ofReal c for every k.

1. Case W = ∅. Take c := 0 (so ofReal c = 0). For each k, ∫⁻_∅ ‖u_k‖ₑ = 0 because μ.restrict ∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty). Also b_k = 0: by definition b_k is the supremum, over compactly supported Lipschitz fields g with tsupport g ⊆ ∅ and sup-norm ≤ 1, of ofReal(∫_∅ u_k · div g dx); every such Bochner integral is taken against the zero measure μ.restrict ∅ = 0, hence equals 0, and ofReal 0 = 0; a supremum of zeros (or an empty supremum) in [0,∞] is 0. (In Lean: simp [Chapter02.bvVariationOn].) Both required bounds hold.

2. Case W ≠ ∅. Then 0 < μ(W): W is open and nonempty and Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpen.measure_pos; for n = 0 the space is a single point of measure 1). And μ(W) < ∞ by hypothesis. So μ(W) ≠ 0 and μ(W) ≠ ∞.

3. Fix k. The function x ↦ b_k is constant, hence measurable, so by lintegral_add_right and setLIntegral_const
   ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + b_k) dx = ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + b_k · μ(W).
   This quantity is one of the terms of the supremum S, so (le_iSup) ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + b_k · μ(W) ≤ S.

4. From step 3 (both summands are ≤ their sum in [0,∞]): ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ S and b_k · μ(W) ≤ S. Since μ(W) ≠ 0 and μ(W) ≠ ∞, ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le turns the second inequality into b_k ≤ S / μ(W).

5. Put C := S + S/μ(W) ∈ [0,∞]. C < ∞: S < ∞ by hypothesis and S/μ(W) < ∞ by ENNReal.div_lt_top (S ≠ ∞, μ(W) ≠ 0). Let c := C.toReal ≥ 0; since C ≠ ∞, ofReal c = C (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).

6. For every k: ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ S ≤ S + S/μ(W) = ofReal c and b_k ≤ S/μ(W) ≤ S + S/μ(W) = ofReal c (steps 4 and 5). Together with c ≥ 0 this is the claim. ∎
key_steps: W = ∅: both integrals vanish (μ.restrict ∅ = 0), and bvVariationOn _ ∅ = 0 since every term of its supremum is ofReal 0; take c = 0.
W ≠ ∅: 0 < Lⁿ(W) < ∞ (open nonempty set for a Haar measure; hypothesis).
ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le: b_k ≤ S/Lⁿ(W); C := S + S/Lⁿ(W) < ∞.
c := C.toReal ≥ 0 with ofReal c = C bounds both quantities for every k.
